purpose: Register of the anchors used by papers/artifacts/w30/composite-laminate-verification/laminate_anchor_closure.json. Every entry is graded here, including the ones that could not be acquired. No numeric value in this file is transcribed from memory: values are either (a) derived by benchmarks/composite_laminate_w30/symbolic_anchor.py, or (b) quoted verbatim from a document whose bytes were retrieved and hashed in this session.

grade_legend.DERIVED-EXACT: computed here at 60-digit mpmath precision from the classical CLT formulation and the declared inputs; reproducible by re-running the generator (self-hashed)
grade_legend.CALIBRATION-IDENTITY: an exact algebraic consequence of the criterion definition (a uni-axially loaded lamina has index exactly 1); no numbers involved
grade_legend.SECONDARY-QUALITATIVE: public document retrieved and hashed in this session that attests the *usage* of the criterion; it contains no numeric constants usable as a value anchor
grade_legend.WITHHELD: the document could not be retrieved from this sandbox; the attempted channels and their HTTP outcomes are recorded and no value is claimed
grade_legend.NOT_SUPPORTED: the source does not contain the required clause at all (verified against the in-repo transcript)

entries.subject: classical lamination theory ABD and transverse-shear stiffness of the four layups

provenance.method: Q = S^-1 (compliance inversion), Qbar = T^-1 Q R (transformation matrices), exact thickness integration, 60-digit mpmath; precision stability 3.44e-62 relative between 60 and 90 digits
provenance.independence_check: agrees with the classical power-formula route (clt_independent.transformed_reduced) to 3e-16 relative and with TensorFEM's rotated-3-D condensation to 4e-14 relative

entries.material_note: elastic constants are TensorFEM's in-repo IM7/8552 Ply3D (src/tensorfem/composite_laminate_bending.py); no strength data required for this entry

entries.subject: mid-surface strains, ply stresses and Tsai-Wu / Tsai-Hill / maximum-stress indices per ply

provenance.criterion_formulation: Tsai & Wu (1971) quadratic form with F1=1/Xt-1/Xc, F2=1/Yt-1/Yc, F11=1/(Xt Xc), F22=1/(Yt Yc), F66=1/S^2, F12=F12*/sqrt(F11 F22), F12*=-1/2; Tsai-Hill with X, Y switched on the sign of the stress; maximum stress as the max of the three component ratios
provenance.load_cases: uniaxial tension 1e6 N/m, biaxial 5e5/5e5 N/m, pure shear 5e5 N/m, uniaxial compression -1e6 N/m

entries.honesty_note: the *formulation* is standard; the coefficient values inside these indices depend on the declared strength allowables (entry LAM-STRENGTH-INPUTS, WITHHELD). All cross-path comparisons in the closure are exactly homogeneous in those allowables, so the comparison conclusion does not inherit this gap.

entries.subject: criterion calibration identities: index = 1 under each allowable state

provenance.algebra: Tsai-Wu: (1/Xt - 1/Xc)Xt + Xt^2/(Xt Xc) = 1 identically, and likewise for the other three states

entries.subject: ply strength allowables Xt, Xc, Yt, Yc, S
entries.status: These five numbers are a DECLARED INPUT. They were not retrieved from a document in this sandbox: no open copy of a composite material handbook could be fetched (see retrieval_log). They are declared here so that the artifact is reproducible, and every compared quantity in the closure is either independent of them (A, B, D, strains, stresses) or exactly homogeneous in them (failure index, FPF load factor) -- scaling all five by a factor s scales every index by s or s^2 and every load factor by 1/s, identically on the anchor and on both solver paths.
entries.risk_if_wrong: the absolute magnitudes of the reported indices are material-specific and would change with a different allowables set; the PASS/FAIL of the closure criteria would not
